raw_response:
I am 73 years old and I only finished primary school. I have farmed these 4.1 mu in Quzhou County for 50 years, doing winter wheat and summer maize just like my neighbors. My farm is small, and every bag of fertilizer is real money out of my pocket, but a bad harvest is worse. I would rather put on a little too much than risk empty grain heads.

For wheat this year, I will sow the same improved variety I used last year — the kind they sell at the supply shop. Before sowing in October, I will rotary till the field and spread base fertilizer: about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu. Then in March when the wheat turns green, I will topdress with urea, almost a full bag per mu by the time I am done. That is a heavy hand, maybe 80 or 90 jin of urea per mu in total, but Old Wang down the road did that and his wheat stood strong. I will irrigate three times: once before winter if the soil is dry, once at green-up, and once when the grain is filling. Pumping costs electricity, but three times is what we have always done. I will spray twice: once for weeds after sowing, and once in spring for aphids or rust if I see them. If the weather is normal I expect about 900 jin per mu.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. I use hybrid seed — everyone does now — about 3 jin per mu. I do not have time or energy to plow deep, and the season is short, so I plant no-tillage into the wheat stubble. I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting, about half a bag per mu, then when the corn is knee-high I add urea, about 40 jin per mu. That is a good amount of nitrogen. I will irrigate twice: once when the stalks are shooting up, and once when the tassels and silks come out. July rains sometimes help, but I do not count on them. I spray twice: once for weeds, and once for corn borer. If the weather holds I expect 1,100 jin per mu.

I do not hire labor. It is just me and my wife. We watch our neighbors and do what they do. If the people around me apply a certain amount, I apply about the same. Change is risky, and at my age I stick to what I know. I spend what I must on fertilizer and irrigation, because skimping is how you end up with a disaster.
